Extol

/ɪkˈstoʊl/ — ik-STOLE, rhymes with stole · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To extol something is to praise it highly and enthusiastically.

The coach extolled the team's discipline after their flawless performance.

Worked Example

At the awards ceremony, the principal took the microphone and spoke glowingly about the debate team's rigorous preparation, their eloquent arguments, and their unwavering commitment to excellence.

Extol captures the enthusiastic, sustained PRAISE and CELEBRATION of the team's qualities. 'Praise' alone is too generic; extol specifically means to celebrate something highly and publicly in a way that highlights its virtues.

How Extol Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

praise

praise: to say good things about something

commend

commend: to praise formally or officially

acclaim

acclaim: to praise loudly and publicly

Antonyms

criticize

disparage

disparage: to talk something down as worthless

How Strong Is It? — mention → praise → commend → extol

mention vs. extol

mention vs. extol: Mention is the weakest action on this scale: to mention something is merely to bring it up, while to extol it is to praise it lavishly and enthusiastically.

praise vs. extol

praise vs. extol: Praise is stronger than a mere mention, but extol is stronger still — praise says 'well done,' while to extol is to heap on glowing, enthusiastic tribute.

commend vs. extol

commend vs. extol: Commend is formal, measured praise, yet extol outdoes it: a teacher commends solid work, but extols a performance she can't stop raving about.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — ex-

Prefix — ex-: up, out (Latin)

Root — tol (tollere)

Root — tol (tollere): to lift, raise (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Ex- means 'up, out' and tol- comes from Latin tollere, 'to lift or raise' — to extol someone is literally to 'lift them up' with high, enthusiastic praise.

Use the root in a new word: tolerate

Use the root in a new word: tolerate: When you tolerate a heavy workload you 'carry' it — the same Latin family of tol- ('lift, bear') that makes extol mean lifting someone high with praise.

Root Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Extol is the word for enthusiastic, effusive praise — when you want to celebrate someone's or something's excellence publicly. For mild approval, use 'praise' or 'approve.' For an official commendation, 'commend' fits better.
